change_unit.title: Recover interrupted Codex sessions into one review packet
change_unit.executive_summary: Turns fragmented across planner, implementer, and reviewer sessions are now surfaced as one coherent change unit with a stable diff, a guided tutorial, and a next proposed chunk.
change_unit.tutorial_markdown:
## What changed

This packet makes the app feel like a review cockpit instead of a raw transcript browser. The selected change unit now owns the summary, tutorial, diff, linked sessions, verdicts, and the next proposed chunk.

## Why it matters

Previously, you had to reconstruct the story by bouncing between session logs. This change moves the explanation layer to the top and keeps the session replay as supporting evidence off to the side.

## What to review

- Make sure the replay panel still preserves role order: planner, implementer, reviewer A, reviewer B.
- Confirm the diff stays first-class and does not collapse into a footer.
- Check that the next proposed chunk reads like an actionable handoff, not a generic note.

## Expected outcome

A reviewer should be able to open the page, skim the executive summary, inspect the diff, replay the sessions, and decide whether the next chunk is safe to approve.
change_unit.next_prompt:
Take the same `change_unit` model and add a live Codex refresh path for linked sessions that already have `thread_id`s.

Requirements:
1. Reuse the existing bundle/session model instead of inventing a second transcript shape.
2. Pull turns from Codex app-server and map them into the replay panel fields already in use.
3. Keep the review surface usable even when the Codex bridge fails; treat live refresh as additive, not foundational.
